title: Can wildlife monitoring power cover its own overhead?
boundary: Declared synthetic steady-load sizing model for an off-grid wildlife-crossing monitoring cluster. No measured wildlife or site data, animal response, transient load, electrical protection, charging, reliability, construction sequence or safety approval is modelled. Hot is a declared scenario, not an uncertainty distribution or universal worst case.

physicalAssumptions.usableEnergy: Net DC energy available after cell-internal losses; converter losses and cooling electricity are accounted separately.
physicalAssumptions.batteryHeat: Synthetic thermal design allowance per operating pack; not a claim that actual heat must increase whenever packs are added at a fixed load.
physicalAssumptions.converterLoss: Constant design allowance per operating unit, counted as both battery energy demand and heat to remove.
physicalAssumptions.operation: All selected power-support units operate throughout the declared monitoring period at a constant load. Cameras, sensors, illumination, a data link and a logger are represented by one aggregate load; their individual performance and any charging are outside this model.
physicalAssumptions.cabinetVolume: Positive, additive cabinet-volume allocations in litres, including an invented allowance for each unit housing and internal spacing. These are not ground footprint, exterior cabinet dimensions, a packing calculation, or measured product volumes.

scenarioMapping.powerAndEnergy: Numerical catalogue ratings retained, physical magnitudes divided by 1000: kW becomes W, kWh becomes Wh. All three interface inequalities are recomputed with the pinned package.
scenarioMapping.capital: Every equipment capital coefficient divided by 1000, in GBP.
scenarioMapping.cabinetVolume: New synthetic cabinet-volume allocations use the historical area coefficient numbers as litres; this is a new declared resource relation, not conversion from square metres to litres.
scenarioMapping.unchanged: Integer counts, availability caps, hours, condition factors and the feedback structure are retained for a comparable numerical experiment.
